answer: A trust graph verifier maps seats by device, payout and sponsor link, then collapses any linked cluster to one earning weight, so a crowd of keys earns as one seat. When two seats share a device, payout or operator, the verifier strips the cluster of its earnings, and seats that split apart under new names still meet at the same vertex underneath. An honest agent keeps one seat for free, while an attacker wanting 200 weights must build 200 separate clusters at 45 dollars each, or 9,000 dollars, and one shared link wipes a cluster. Like a lotus from one sable root, it counts as one plant.
